verdicts.quote: If and only if every row is valid, all rows are created together as one atomic unit ... If anything fails, no user from the file exists afterwards.
rejection (file errors *or* row errors with row numbers, field and code, and a message the admin can act on). ... All row errors for the file are reported

checked case-insensitively ... against (a) all existing user records of any status and (b) earlier rows in the same file. ... every later occurrence is `DUPLICATE_IN_FILE` ... Existing users are never updated (no upsert).
Each created user has ... the default non-admin role (A-3) ... the CSV can set nothing else. ... Admin role can never be granted by import (there is no role column, R-3).
The import endpoint and page are available to a caller whose *current* role is admin. Everyone else is refused before the file is read.
verdicts.missing: Whether the import ability is a distinct permission from single-user creation, i.e. that being able to create one user does not imply being able to bulk-import.

verdicts.quote: The first record is a header. ... Exactly the set {email, name}; any other header, a missing required header, or a repeated header (after normalisation) is a file error.
a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is accepted and ignored. Lines may end in LF or CRLF. Fields follow RFC 4180 quoting (quoted fields may contain commas, doubled quotes, line breaks).
No email is sent by this feature.
at most `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` data records and at most `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` bytes (R-2). ... Exactly `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` rows is accepted; one more → 400 `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, nothing created
zero bytes or only blank lines → 400 `EMPTY_FILE`. ... [R-3] A header-only file → 400 `NO_DATA_ROWS`. ... [R-2.1] `FX-BOM` ... → 201, user `fred@example.com` / `Fred Ford` created.
After `FX-OK3` succeeded (Store has 7 users), submitting the identical file again → 422 with `ALREADY_EXISTS` on rows 1, 2, 3; Store still 7.
Background/asynchronous import of very large files | R-9 | Synchronous only, bounded by the limits of R-9. ... [§3.1] the response *is* the completion signal
The feature sends no message.
Imported users are created without a usable credential and reach the product through the existing "set/reset password" or invite mechanism.
verdicts.missing: Whether the created account is active or pending, and the concrete first sign-in path (left open as G-2).

verdicts.quote: the uploaded file is not persisted (no temp file survives the request)
Exactly the set {email, name}; any other header ... is a file error.
verdicts.missing: No explicit statement of locale-dependent value handling (e.g. Unicode normalisation of names or locale-specific case folding); the closed column set only implies no date/number values exist.

verdicts.quote: Each attempt after authorization writes one audit entry (A-8) so an admin action can be traced ... the audit entry holds admin id, timestamp, outcome, counts and error codes only
Imports have no partial-success state (A-5). ... After a fault the admin may resubmit the same file safely.
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled; retrying only failed rows is implicitly moot under atomicity but cancellation is not addressed.

verdicts.quote: a maximum response time for a file at the limit are **unresolved** ... [R-10] *pending* (submit disabled, "Importing…" status, file control locked
verdicts.missing: The actual time bound for a maximum-size file, and any progress indication beyond an indeterminate 'Importing…' status.

verdicts.quote: **Preserved:** every existing user's data and the existing single-user creation behavior
names that begin with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` are stored verbatim and any future CSV export must neutralise them ... row messages never reflect raw field values into HTML unescaped.
